subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound media staging?
rationale: The code proof is strong, but the patch deliberately extends a trusted local HTML host-read boundary beyond the temp root; automation can check fail-closed mechanics but cannot own that security boundary decision.

options.title: Accept Provenance Boundary
options.body: Approve the sha256/size-bound SQLite provenance design and land after exact-head CI on current main.

options.title: Request Narrower Lifecycle
options.body: Ask for additional lifecycle constraints such as TTL/chunked pruning or broader upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Pause For Redesign
options.body: Reject outbound-staged HTML trust for now and require a different delivery path that avoids expanding host-read HTML acceptance.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance Boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the sha256/size-bound SQLite provenance design and land after exact-head CI on current main.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the original trusted generated HTML seam and the SQLite state foundation that this PR builds on.
